industry.cdmoGlobal: Global pharma CDMO market ~US$197.4 bn in 2025, projected ~US$368.7 bn by 2034 (7.15% CAGR) (AR FY26 MD&A, citing industry reports)
industry.apiGlobal: Global API market ~US$270.5 bn in 2025 to ~US$419 bn by 2033 (5.55% CAGR); synthetic small molecules still the bulk (AR FY26 MD&A)
industry.adc: 22 ADCs approved globally by May-2026 (14 by the US FDA); ADC sales ~US$16.1 bn in 2025 (Enhertu US$5.0 bn, Padcev US$3.0 bn, Adcetris US$1.6 bn); ADC contract manufacturing ~US$8.9 bn (2024) to ~US$16.5 bn (2030), ~10.9% a year; bioconjugation CDMO ~US$2.2 bn (2025) to ~US$4.4 bn (2030), ~15% a year (AR FY26 MD&A)
industry.oligo: Oligonucleotide CDMO ~US$0.91 bn (2024) to ~US$3.16 bn (2033), ~15% a year (AR FY26 MD&A); company deck: oligo market US$1 bn (FY24) to US$4 bn (FY29E)
industry.specialty: Global specialty chemicals ~US$941 bn (2025) to ~US$1,377 bn (2035), 3.5% CAGR; agrochemicals in a global downturn with Chinese generic price pressure (AR FY26; q1call)
industry.china: US de-risking from Chinese suppliers (Department of Defense list naming Chinese CDMOs; BIOSECURE-type legislation) is lifting late-stage RFQs to Indian CDMOs, but customers already have one or two sources, so conversion is slow (Cohance CDMO CEO, q1call)

moat.evidence: Top 20 innovators give >85% of small-molecule revenue; 30-year Suven relationships; but 'a lot of these customers did not necessarily increase the width of their business with us in the past 2 to 3 years' (Umang Vohra) and two commercial molecules destocked
Top-3 global position in 8 of the top 10 API molecules; >50% share with some innovators; controlled substances (regulatory entry barrier); gross margin ~71%
Early: niche technologies 15-16% of revenue; NJ Bio loses ~₹50 cr a quarter before minorities; Sapala is small (₹27 cr in Q1FY27) but growing fast
Warning Letter at Nacharam (Feb-2026), Form 483 with five observations at Pashamylaram (Aug-2026); Jaggaiahpet clean
3,000+ kL across 15 sites, backward integration in APIs; utilisation is low after the FY26-27 revenue fall
Executive Chairman, MD, CEO and CFO all changed between Oct-2025 and Sep-2026; the new chairman calls the churn a reason peers 'moved faster than Cohance'

critiques: The merger was sold as a CDMO platform with a US$1 bn revenue target at mid-30s margins by FY30; 17 months later revenue is 13% lower (FY26), Q1FY27 EBITDA margin is 0.3% and the target is 'an aspiration'.

Earnings have collapsed: attributable EPS ₹12.68 (FY25, restated) to ₹4.68 (FY26) to a loss in Q1FY27; the reported loss would be twice as large without NJ Bio's minority partners absorbing 44% of its losses.
NJ Bio (₹548 cr for 56% plus a put option on the rest) loses ~₹50 cr a quarter; its goodwill test assumes 24% revenue growth and a lower discount rate (10.1% vs 10.7%).
API+ is now ~60% of sales; BOBCAPS calls it an industry-low-margin mix for a CDMO and values the stock at 40x for that reason.
Advent controls 57.49% and has pledged 54.36% of the company for a US$285 mn holdco loan; Advent sold 8.92% at ~₹906 in Sep-2025 to repay holdco debt. A further sell-down is an overhang.
Leadership churn: four senior exits in eleven months; the CFO left on 13-Sep-2026 with no successor named by 30-Sep.
Quality: a US FDA Warning Letter (Nacharam) and a Form 483 at a key CDMO site (Pashamylaram) in the same year.
gaps: Segment EBITDA is not disclosed (one audited segment); segment margins in this report are our inference from standalone vs subsidiary data.
Customer concentration by molecule or customer is not disclosed (management declined on the Q4FY26 call); the two destocked molecules are not named.
Broker methods: only BOBCAPS's is in the material we could access; ICICI Securities, Jefferies, Goldman Sachs and Macquarie methods and EPS are not.
JP Morgan initiated at Overweight (₹1,300) in 2025; its standing view on 30-Sep-2026 is not in our sources. The ₹280 consensus low target is not attributed.
Jun-2026 named holders: the AR gives Mar-2026 holders above 5% only; mutual-fund holdings are not itemised in our sources.
NJ Bio and Sapala quarterly P&L below EBITDA are not disclosed; our NJ Bio pre-tax loss (~₹48 cr in Q1FY27) is derived from the NCI share and consolidated vs standalone D&A and finance cost.
Raisin Aggregator LP (₹260 cr) is described only as an unquoted US equity investment; its underlying business is not stated in the AR.
Timing and price of the minority buy-outs (Sapala tranches, NJ Bio put) are not disclosed beyond 'full ownership of Sapala by FY30'.
conflicts: FY25 EPS: Screener ₹19.14 (restated profit over pre-merger shares) vs AR ₹12.79 basic / ₹12.68 diluted; we use the AR (COHANCE.patch.js).
Q1FY27 loss: ₹24.1 cr (attributable) vs ₹45.2 cr (before minorities); both are correct on their basis; our EPS is attributable.
FY26 segment growth: deck text says API+ -8.0% and Spec Chem -2.1%, matching the restated chart (API+ ₹1,182.6 cr to ₹1,088.0 cr); the restated split differs from the quarterly decks.
Goldman Sachs target reported as ₹500 (post-Q1 summary) and ₹525 (an earlier raise); we use ₹500 as the later.
Exceptional items FY25: AR charge ₹15.78 cr (compounding fees) vs Screener's positive 'exceptional' ₹25.2 cr; we use the AR.
